test_name: 200 editable general claims: top 1 through top 10

recommendation.rule: highest exact macro F1, then highest exact accuracy, then smallest k

notes: 200 source-labelled general claims across 10 categories; 100 SUPPORTS and 100 REFUTES. Labels/sources are fixed in the editable Python CLAIMS list before inference.

Related true/false examples share a group and remain in one split. The selection split contains 100 claims (50 per label); 100 claims (50 per label) form a reserved check split. Every category is balanced by label in both splits.
Every claim is independently retrieved once using the existing hybrid BM25/MiniLM ranking. Top k uses the first k passages of that claim-specific top-ten ranking.

Rendered passages are deduplicated and newline-joined exactly as in the application. The existing BERT adapter repeats claims across lossless evidence chunks, averages raw chunk logits and then applies softmax. All 2,000 predictions are newly computed.
k is frozen using selection-only exact macro F1, then accuracy, then smaller k before any check predictions are computed. Check and combined results never reselect k.

This expanded diagnostic reuses earlier evaluated claims and adds further claims after observing earlier pipeline results. It is not an unbiased test set or an independently held-out FEVER benchmark. Training-data overlap and semantic evidence sufficiency have not been assessed; the reserved split is only an internal check.

A correct label without sufficient evidence is not successful verification. Confidence is BERT's binary model confidence, not a probability that a claim is true. Explanations, citation grounding and NOT ENOUGH INFO behavior are not evaluated.

Per-k timing uses measured top-ten retrieval plus BERT classification for that prefix; it is not a separately measured top-k retrieval endpoint. Load times are separate. No warm-up predictions are excluded; early calls can include kernel/caching overhead. CUDA is synchronized around measured operations when used.

All inference uses local, read-only model/index assets with Hugging Face offline mode. No OpenAI/Claude calls, key reads, training, index rebuilding or app setting changes are made. The application default remains five; users may choose one through ten.
